dimension_grades.evidence: The email contains no hedges like 'no worries if not' or 'even if this isn't a fit' — it states the goal directly.
"Are you open to a 30-minute call the week of the 14th?" is a plain, specific ask.
"I want to raise our Series A with Gradient Ventures leading. That's why I'm writing." is completely transparent about intent.
No sentence reads as disguised persuasion; even the personalization section is substantive and directly tied to business evidence rather than manufactured candor.
"When we launched eighteen months ago… three of our first ten customers… We crossed $2.1M in ARR last quarter, up from $400K twelve months prior" places metrics in a clear time-based progression.
All traction data ($2.1M ARR, $400K, 145% NRR, 60% of new revenue) is embedded in flowing prose sentences, not listed as bullets or standalone figures.
The description of the referral loop accounting for 60% of new revenue and the default-to-Fieldwork dynamic lets the reader extrapolate continued compounding growth without the sender claiming it.

"three of our first ten customers started pulling us into their subcontractor networks" and "we expected to spend our first year pushing… Instead" explicitly show customer pull rather than company push.
"Your talk at SaaStr last October on 'workflow gravity'" references a specific talk with a specific concept.
The email connects Sarah's "workflow gravity" thesis — the system of record teams can't route around — directly to Fieldwork's referral loop and default-adoption dynamic.
The personalization passage introduces concrete metrics: the referral loop accounting for 60% of new revenue and 145% NRR as evidence of the "gravity" thesis.
The reference to Sarah's talk flows directly into the origin story and traction narrative in the same paragraph, rather than sitting as a separate flattery block.
The email contains no phrases like 'happy to work around your schedule' or 'whenever works for you' — it proposes a specific time window directly.

The email frames the conversation as James walking Sarah through his business ("I'd like to walk you through the full picture") but does not imply why the conversation would be valuable or interesting for Sarah beyond the implicit investment opportunity.
"Are you open to a 30-minute call the week of the 14th?" proposes a concrete time window and duration.
"$2.1M ARR in vertical SaaS for construction" includes a concrete traction signal and domain in the subject line.
"Series A conversation" makes the purpose of the email immediately discernible from the subject line.
The subject line uses standard capitalization and plain language with no ellipses, vague teasers, or 're:' faking.
